fullPassage: People like pictures of the savanna, even if they have never been there. In one study, people of different ages (8, 11, 15, 18, 35, and over 70 years) looked at images of tropical forests, deciduous forests, coniferous forests, deserts, and the East African savanna. Eight-year-old children said that they would like to live in or visit the savanna more than any other environment. After the age of 15, people also liked deciduous and coniferous forests. Since none of these people had visited savannas, the implication is that this preference was programmed into their brains. This programmed preference is called "the savanna hypothesis." As people get older, this preference gets modified by where they have lived. Synek and Grammer, researchers in evolutionary psychology, confirmed these findings in a different study. They showed that young children in Austria prefer landscapes thinly dotted with trees and with low mountains, scenes that resemble the savanna. After puberty, their preferences shifted to areas with denser trees and higher mountains, again, presumably, because of more experience with these terrains.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 shifted와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① transferred: transferred(옮겨진)는 shifted와 유사한 의미
✅ ② remained: remained(남아 있었다/유지되었다)는 shifted(변했다/이동했다)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ③ altered: altered(변한)는 shifted와 유사한 의미
❌ ④ evolved: evolved(진화한)는 shifted와 유사한 의미
det.tip: shifted(변했다/이동했다) ↔ remained(유지되었다) — 변화 vs 유지의 대조

questions.passage: People like pictures of the savanna, even if they have never been there. In one study, people of different ages (8, 11, 15, 18, 35, and over 70 years) looked at images of tropical forests, deciduous forests, coniferous forests, deserts, and the East African savanna. Eight-year-old children said that they would like to live in or visit the savanna more than any other environment. After the age of 15, people also liked deciduous and coniferous forests. Since none of these people had visited savannas, the implication is that this preference was programmed into their brains. This programmed preference is called "the savanna hypothesis." As people get older, this preference gets modified by where they have lived. Synek and Grammer, researchers in evolutionary psychology, confirmed these findings in a different study. They showed that young children in Austria prefer landscapes thinly dotted with trees and with low mountains, scenes that resemble the savanna. After puberty, their preferences shifted to areas with <u>denser</u> trees and higher mountains, again, presumably, because of more experience with these terrains.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 denser와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① thicker: thicker(더 두꺼운)는 denser와 유사한 의미
❌ ② heavier: heavier(더 무거운)는 denser의 반의어가 아님
✅ ③ sparser: sparser(더 드문/성긴)는 denser(더 밀집한)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ④ richer: richer(더 풍부한)는 denser와 다른 차원의 의미
det.tip: denser(더 밀집한) ↔ sparser(더 성긴/드문) — 밀도의 대조

questions.passage:
(A) The doctor will <u>visit</u> the patient at home every week to check on her recovery.
(B) Eight-year-old children said that they would like to live in or <u>visit</u> the savanna more than any other environment.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 visit의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: visit: (A) 의사가 환자를 방문하다 / (B) 사바나를 가보다/여행하다
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 방문하다 — (B) 여행하다/가보다: (A)는 의사가 환자의 집을 방문하는 의미, (B)는 사바나에 가보고 싶다는 여행/방문의 의미로 다의어의 두 용법을 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ② (A) 치료하다 — (B) 탐험하다: visit에 치료하다는 의미 없음
❌ ③ (A) 방문하다 — (B) 거주하다: (B)에서 live in과 or로 병렬이므로 거주와 다른 의미여야 함
❌ ④ (A) 진찰하다 — (B) 관찰하다: visit에 진찰하다/관찰하다는 의미 없음
det.tip: visit: ① (사람/장소를) 방문하다 ② (관광 등의 목적으로) 가보다/여행하다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a suggested explanation for something that has not yet been proved"

det.korean: hypothesis=가설 (아직 증명되지 않은 것에 대한 제안된 설명)
det.analysis:
❌ ① experiment: experiment(실험)은 증명 과정이지 설명 자체가 아님
✅ ② hypothesis: hypothesis(가설)는 아직 증명되지 않은 제안된 설명으로 영영 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ conclusion: conclusion(결론)은 이미 도출된 결과이므로 '아직 증명되지 않은'과 맞지 않음
❌ ④ observation: observation(관찰)은 설명이 아니라 사실 확인에 해당
det.tip: hypothesis = 가설. 본문: the savanna hypothesis(사바나 가설)

questions.passage: Since none of these people had visited savannas, the __________ (imply) is that this preference was programmed into their brains. This programmed preference is called "the savanna hypothesis."

det.analysis: imply(동사) → implication(명사). the __________ is 구조에서 주어 자리이므로 명사형 implication이 필요. imply → implication(명사 변환)
det.tip: the implication is that — 암시하는 바는 ~이다. imply → implication (명사 변환)
